run: run 1 of up to 3: M's continuations, then nine fits in order C0a, C0b, two C2, five C1, each read by the spec 3.7 rule; run 2 (the trained sides) files its own rules and opens only as spec 5 says
filed: 2026-11-23, before the $0 rehearsal; thresholds.full.c0a_rn_dev is filled from the rehearsal's C0a deviation before run 1 and the file is committed then, never edited after run 1 starts
plan: reports/plans/2026-11-23_plan_p2-72-delta-crosscoder-spec.md (the spec, reviewed three rounds); run plan reports/plans/2026-11-23_plan_p2-72-run.md
kind: descriptive: the method as published, one label per side (yes / no / not scored); no reuse score, no share column (whip-lead, spec header)

rehearsal.dead_tokens_source: rehearsal only: 200k tokens (about 49 steps) so the AuxK path runs inside 1,500 steps, as E235's rehearsal lowered it

arch.expansion_source: paper 4.2 'We use an expansion factor of 5' -> 3,840 latents
arch.shared_frac_source: paper 3.3 and Table 1 'Shared Features Fraction | 20%' -> 768 shared, 3,072 non-shared
arch.k_shared_source: ours, a choice (spec 3.2, departures row 'budgets'): alpha = 0.5 from Table 1's 'Shared k Multiplier 2.0' (an inference), and each block's active fraction of the paper's Llama width (400 of 4,096 shared, 200 of 16,384 non-shared): 768 x 400/4096 = 75 -> 76 = 2 x 38
arch.lam_delta_source: Appendix A 'We set the delta loss weight Δλ=0.005'
arch.aux_alpha_source: Table 1 'AuxK Coefficient (α_auxk) | 1/32'; its form is Minder's AuxK (trainers/crosscoder.py 421-480), our reading of lambda_s under BatchTopK (spec 3.3)
arch.dead_tokens_source: paper Appendix B: dead after 10M tokens without firing (Minder's default too)
arch.target_rms_source: Minder's normaliser target (E235 settings.cc.full.target_rms 100, from diffing-toolkit@617d926 configs/diffing/method/crosscoder.yaml), applied as one scalar fit on M with no mean subtraction (spec 3.1)

rehearsal.sizes_source: rehearsal: the full dictionary, batch and generation batch (so ms per step, the sampler's tokens per second and the C0a bf16 deviation are measured as run 1 meets them), 1,500 steps, 4,000 prompts, one candidate and an 8-latent pool on 32 Pile-loss rows; the `slice` job reads one candidate with the full 60-latent pool at the full read sizes

sizes.steps_source: Table 1 'Total Training Steps | 50,000', 'Batch Size | 4096': 204.8M token presentations, the paper's 'approximately 200 million tokens'; one pass, no k annealing (spec 3.4)
sizes.warmup_source: Table 1 'Warmup Steps | 1,000', then constant (no decay stated)
sizes.prompts_source: paper 4.2: 200,000 prompts, 100,000 answered by the base and 100,000 by the fine-tune (spec 3.5)
sizes.prompt_len_source: ours: 20M contrastive tokens over 200,000 prompts is 100 tokens a row (paper 4.2); position 0 is dropped as E203/E235 drop it, so each row is 33 prompt tokens and 68 sampled ones and gives exactly 100 activations (32 prompt, 68 continuation: the spec's 6.4M prompt tokens inside 20.0M)
sizes.f_share_source: spec 3.5: the fit-half quota 40.96M, 20% of 204.8M, Pile filling any shortfall
sizes.pre_rows_source: spec 3.5: Pile train rows 400,000-761,999, one pass (362,000 rows x 511 = 184.98M activations, enough for C0's 184.8M)
sizes.n_chunks_source: ours: 1.024M tokens a chunk, about E235's 1,024-row chunk, so a chunk of both models' activations fits beside the crosscoder
sizes.gen_batch_source: ours; the rehearsal measures the sampler at this batch (spec 3.6)
sizes.check_step_source: spec 5 'Expected at 1k steps: FVE at least 0.5, and L_delta falling'
sizes.candidates_source: paper 4.3: 'select the top-3 latents from the right tail'
sizes.pool_source: spec 3.7: 60 bulk latents per candidate; under 60, widen; under 20, 'not scored'
sizes.pile_loss_rows_source: spec 3.5: Pile validation rows 0-255 for the Pile loss
sizes.read_batch_source: spec 3.2: inference batch top-K on shuffled batches of 4,096 read tokens

run.sites_source: spec 3.1: A block 2's input (E203/E235's site A, the paper's middle layer), B the last block's output, for the block-3 head and C2 at B only
run.fits_source: spec 5 run 1: C0a identical models, paired init (wiring); C0b identical, independent init (null band); C2 E235's Gaussian matched to e54 elicit s0's activation change at A and at B (E235's G1: crosscoder_proper run.py `gauss`, draw 0); C1 E243 rung 1 and rung 5 (crosscoder_proper run2.py: E206's early head scaled to the rung's size at A), E212's planted direction (realistic_tasks run3.py `planted`), E235's block-3 head (graft_sites last_lowest at B), rung 5 with tied shared decoders (spec appendix 2)
run.temperature_source: Appendix C 'Temperature: 0.7', 'Top-p: 0.9' (spec 3.5 applies them to the contrastive continuations)
run.strengths_source: Appendix C 's∈{−200,−100,−80,−50,−20,0,20,50,80,100,200}', the nonzero ten, uncapped (spec 3.7); added as s * rho / 100 times the unit d^ft, rho the median per-token norm of M at the site on the Pile-loss rows (ours, for 'model-specific normalization factors')
run.widen_source: spec 3.7: |d^ft| within 1.5 and firing rate within 2, then 2 and 4, then 3 and 8
run.top_n_source: spec 3.7: the candidate's 50 most activating tokens
run.contexts_source: spec 3.7: 20 top contexts per candidate saved for a reader
run.alive_min_source: E235's alive_min (crosscoder_proper settings.cc.full): fired at least 10 times on the eval set (the Pile background plus the side's score windows)
run.seeds_source: new for this run, except plant_seed: E212's (realistic_tasks predictions_run3.json settings.plant_seed), so its planted vector is reproduced
run.self_task_source: spec 3.7: C0b's differential null reads E62's copy task (share_untrained inventory e62/copy, induction_cue windows.pt)
run.ranges_source: spec 3.5's table; `check_disjoint` asserts no two overlap before any GPU work
run.graft_window_source: E201/E235 graft windows of 32 tokens from Pile train rows 0-16,383
run.score_tf32_source: ours: the steering and Pile-loss reads run under TF32 (about 3x the fp32 rate), candidate and pool under the same arithmetic; the stream and the plant's norm stay fp32 as E235 ran them

thresholds.thresholds_source: c0a_rn_dev: spec 5, one bar filed after the rehearsal measures max |R - 0.5| of C0a under bf16 on the same kernels (null until then; run.py refuses a full fit while it is null); fve_check: spec 5 'Expected at 1k steps: FVE at least 0.5' (mean batch FVE of the worse model over steps 900-999); fve_min_end: spec 5 'FVE under 0.5 at the end of a fit marks it a code fault' (E235 read at least 0.89, the paper at least 0.72); gen_cap_min, fit_cap_min: spec 5's stage caps (30 min per 100k continuations, 60 min per fit), each projected from the first shard and from step 1,000; score_budget_min: spec 5's scoring estimate (24 min) added to the projected training minutes; score_cap_min: ours, the fit cap less stream and training (about 20 min), projected after the first latent's reads; the rehearsal keeps nothing it cannot meet at 1,500 steps and records every reading

readings.label: per side: yes (one scored candidate beats its pool's maximum on both tests), no (at least one candidate scored, none passes both), not scored (no candidate has a pool of 20 or more)
readings.steer: the steering test's statistic: max over negative s of g_F(0) - g_F(s), absolute nats; g is the answer log-odds on the score windows for task sides (C0b: E62 copy; C2: e54 elicit, the Gaussian's matched side), KL(F_s || M) at the read positions for plants
readings.top: the top-activation test's statistic: share of the latent's 50 most activating tokens (z > 0) on behaviour positions, in a set of the score windows plus as many Pile background tokens
readings.induce: reported only, with the caveat that it is weak evidence of reuse (the added vector can carry the learned content): max over positive s of g_M(s) - g_M(0); for plants g_M(s) = -KL(F || M_s), so this is how far steering moves M toward F
readings.beside: per candidate: R, the pool's maxima, the widening used, the Pile-loss rise of F at every s, 20 contexts; per fit: FVE per model, L0, dead share, the tail (min and max R over non-shared latents) and the ledger; on C1 the other tail's top three by R, read and reported, never scored

C0a wiring (stop).rule: identical models, paired init: the delta loss is exactly 0.0 at every step (a nonzero value stops the run at that step); at the end max over all latents of |R - 0.5| <= c0a_rn_dev; FVE >= fve_min_end. Any miss: exit 1 and no other fit runs (`gate` refuses every key until C0a.json holds done with every check passed).
C0a wiring (stop).expected: delta 0.0 exactly at every step (Delta = 0 since F's activations are M's own, and the two decoders stay equal: every gradient and Adam update is the same on both); R = 0.5 on every latent, a deviation of 0 or bf16 rounding; recovery not read (every latent ties)
C0a wiring (stop).blind_to: anything a real change does; it fails only on a wiring fault (a model mix-up, an asymmetric path)
C0a wiring (stop).edge_cases: a deviation exactly at the bar passes (<=); a nan R (both decoder norms 0, impossible at init 0.4) fails

C0b null band (descriptive).rule: identical models, independent init: the tail min and max of R over non-shared latents, reported beside the paper's 0.492-0.506; recovery read by the label rule on E62's copy log-odds of M (F = M: the steering test asks whether a top-tail latent moves M's own copy log-odds down more than its matched bulk)
C0b null band (descriptive).expected: tail of order 0.49-0.51 (the paper's null 0.492-0.506; our init and width differ, so no bar); label lean 'no', medium (paper 7.1: 'none support causal validation')
C0b null band (descriptive).edge_cases: F = M, so g_F and g_M are one read; every pass compares against the same fit's bulk, so the result is not fixed in advance

C2 random update (gates run 2 at A).rule: the label rule, g = e54 elicit's answer log-odds on its score half (the Gaussian's matched side). C1 fits refuse until both C2 fits have read; a C2 'yes' makes C1 refuse until rerun with --c2-yes-reported (whip-lead told first). It does not cancel C1.
C2 random update (gates run 2 at A).expected: 'no', low confidence at both sites (the paper ran no random control; no prior)
C2 random update (gates run 2 at A).edge_cases: 'not scored' at A: the null was not read and run 2 does not run

C1 planted changes.rule: the label rule, g = KL(F_s || M) at the plant's read positions (heads: every position but 0 of E201's 512 read windows; E212: position 34 of its 512 L1 read rows); the planted direction's cosine with the top candidate's d^ft - d^base reported beside the pool maximum, no bar (E212 only)
C1 planted changes.edge_cases: a plant's KL at s = 0 is > 0 by construction (the graft and the plant write at the site: E235/E243 checked the energy); a steering read giving nan (overflow at s = 200) is skipped in the max over s, and a candidate whose every read is nan cannot pass

pass and label (every side).rule: per candidate, per test: pass iff the candidate's statistic is strictly over the maximum of its pool's statistics (nan pool values skipped; a nan candidate never passes). Pool: alive non-shared latents with |R - 0.5| strictly under the median |R - 0.5| of all non-shared latents, excluding the candidates and the other-tail latents, matched on |d^ft| within 1.5 and firing rate within 2 (then 2/4, then 3/8) until 60 qualify (60 drawn with pool_seed + candidate rank); fewer than 60 at 3/8: all of them if at least 20, else the candidate is not scored. Label: yes / no / not scored as in readings.label.
pass and label (every side).absolute_or_relative: absolute nats for steering; a share for top activations; both ordinal against the same fit's bulk, so no band
pass and label (every side).chance: under exchangeable latents a candidate beats a 60-latent pool on one test with probability 1/61, on both (independent) about 1/3,700; a side with three candidates reads yes by chance with probability about 3/3,700

rules.run 2 gate (run 1's readout): run 2 at site A only if C0a passes, rung 5 or E212 reads yes, and C2 at A reads a calibrated no. No plant yes: site A reads 'not applicable at this update size'. C2 at A not scored: not read. Plant yes and C2 at A yes: 'does not separate a plant from a random update'. Rung 1 decides how a trained side's 'no' reads ('below the method's reach' if rung 1 reads no). The block-3 head and C2 at B gate nothing.
rules.early checks (each fit; stop): before step 0: a matched change within its tolerance (C2: E235's gauss_match_tol 0.05; rungs: E243's match_tol 0.05), the ledger (contrastive + fit half + Pile = steps x batch exactly; disjoint row ranges, asserted at start); every step: finite losses; at check_step: mean batch FVE of the worse model over the 100 steps before >= fve_check, the delta loss's mean over those 100 steps under its mean over the first 100 (not C0a), projected fit minutes <= fit_cap_min; generation: projected minutes per 100k continuations <= gen_cap_min after the first shard; scoring: FVE at the end >= fve_min_end before any steering read, projected steering minutes <= score_cap_min after the first latent

edge_case_checks.label, one scored, none passing: [{scored true, steer true, top false}, {scored false}] -> 'no'
edge_case_checks.label, an unscored candidate that would: [{scored false, steer true, top true}, {scored true, false, false}] -> 'no': an unscored candidate cannot pass
edge_case_checks.pass, nan pool value: beats(0.5, [nan, 0.2]) -> true (nan skipped); beats(0.5, [nan]) -> true (no finite pool value: the pool is not empty, so a finite candidate passes; a pool of 20+ all-nan reads is not expected and is reported in pool_max)
edge_case_checks.pool, zero firing rate: within() is false for a zero rate, so a never-firing latent is never in a pool; candidates are alive (fired >= 10), so their rate is > 0
edge_case_checks.top share, latent firing on fewer than 5: only its firing tokens count, over 50: a latent firing once, on a behaviour position, reads 0.02
edge_case_checks.top share, ties: stable sort: the lower token index first
edge_case_checks.candidates, fewer than 3 alive non-share: returns the alive ones only (no dead latent is a candidate); none alive: no candidate, label 'not scored'
edge_case_checks.do-nothing under the rule: C0b is the do-nothing state read through the rule: a yes there is a false recovery, reported as the null's reading, not a pass

blind_to.label: what a latent means beyond moving g and firing on behaviour positions; how many latents carry the change; a change that sits mostly in shared latents (the method's own ranking cannot see it)
blind_to.steer: behaviour off the score windows; a latent whose d^ft moves g only together with others
blind_to.top: a latent that fires on the behaviour's text but not at the answer positions (heads: every read position is a behaviour position, so the test reads how much more the latent fires on the read windows than on Pile background drawn from the same text distribution)
blind_to.induce: whether the steered vector carries the learned content itself (the spec 1 caveat)
